minor_characters.name: Bulkington
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Glimpsed at the Spouter-Inn (Ch 006) and given a brief eulogistic chapter as helmsman of the Pequod (Ch 026); never speaks again or affects events.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is explicitly a 'stoneless grave' figure with no plot function beyond a thematic meditation on landlessness.

minor_characters.name: Peter Coffin
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Landlord of the Spouter-Inn who jokes about Queequeg and beds Ishmael with him.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His role as comic host can be folded into the Spouter-Inn scene without losing any later reference.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Hussey
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Proprietress of the Try Pots who serves chowder and confiscates Queequeg's harpoon during the Ramadan.
minor_characters.reason_removable: She is local color around the chowder and Ramadan beats and never recurs.

minor_characters.name: Aunt Charity
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Bildad's sister who fusses over Pequod's outfitting and sends ginger aboard.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her bustle adds flavor but no plot consequence; the ginger gag in Ch 075 is self-contained.

minor_characters.name: Elijah
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Ragged 'prophet' on the Nantucket wharves who hints darkly about Ahab to Ishmael and Queequeg.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His ominous foreshadowing duplicates what Peleg, Tistig, and Ahab's own appearance already establish.

minor_characters.name: Dough-Boy
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Pale ship's steward bullied by the harpooneers at the cabin table and elsewhere.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A comic foil for the harpooneers' 'frantic democracy'; removing him does not touch the main arc.

minor_characters.name: Fleece
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Old black cook who delivers the comic sermon to the sharks at Stubb's request in Ch 067.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His sermon is a self-contained set piece with no consequence for plot or main characters.

minor_characters.name: Captain Mayhew
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Captain of the Jeroboam who relays Gabriel's story and Macey's death.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Gabriel and the gam itself (in the synopsis) carry the meaning; Mayhew is a narrative conduit who can be compressed.

minor_characters.name: Harry Macey
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Jeroboam mate killed by Moby Dick, recalled in Gabriel's tale and via the undelivered letter.
minor_characters.reason_removable: An offstage casualty whose function (Moby Dick has killed before) is already covered by Ahab's own history.

minor_characters.name: Derick De Deer
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Bremen captain of the Jungfrau who borrows oil and races the Pequod for a sick old whale.
minor_characters.reason_removable: The Jungfrau gam is in the synopsis, but Derick himself is interchangeable color and can be reduced to 'the German captain.'

minor_characters.name: Steelkilt and Radney
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Lakeman mutineer and Vineyard mate in the embedded Town-Ho story (Ch 057).
minor_characters.reason_removable: They exist only inside a self-contained inset tale that has no bearing on the Pequod's voyage.

minor_characters.name: Cabaco and Archy
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Sailors who overhear Fedallah's hidden crew below decks in Ch 046.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Their eavesdropping merely foreshadows the reveal that the synopsis already gives directly.

minor_characters.name: Captain Sleet
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Fictional Greenland whaler cited at length in the Mast-Head chapter for his crow's-nest.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A digressive citation inside an essayistic chapter, with no narrative role.

minor_characters.name: Old Manxman, Tashtego's senior, Dough-Boy etc. forecastle voices
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Anonymous or near-anonymous sailors who deliver lines in the Midnight Forecastle scene (Ch 043).
minor_characters.reason_removable: The polyglot 'democracy of hands' is established by the synopsis at a glance and need not be dramatized chorus by chorus.

minor_characters.name: Captain Boomer
minor_characters.appearances_summary: One-gam captain of the Samuel Enderby who lost an arm to Moby Dick and tells his tale to Ahab.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His encounter is one more in a series of gam-confirmations of the White Whale; the synopsis names other ships (Jeroboam, Jungfrau, Rachel, Delight) but not this one, and his anecdote can be cut without altering the main arc.

minor_characters.name: Dr. Bunger
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The Samuel Enderby's surgeon who provides comic relief during the gam.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Pure comic byplay attached to a removable gam.

minor_characters.name: Captain Gardiner
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Nantucket captain of the Rachel who begs Ahab to help search for his lost son.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Named here only for completeness; the Rachel encounter is preserved per the synopsis but Gardiner's name itself is incidental.

minor_characters.name: Perth
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The blacksmith with a backstory of ruin who forges Ahab's harpoon.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His personal backstory chapter (The Blacksmith) is digressive; the forging itself must remain but Perth's biography can be excised.

minor_characters.name: Tranquo, king of Tranque
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Mentioned in Ishmael's Arsacides reminiscence about a whale-skeleton temple.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Embedded anecdote with no bearing on the Pequod's voyage.

minor_characters.name: Captain of the Bouton-de-Rose
minor_characters.appearances_summary: French captain duped by Stubb in the ambergris episode.
minor_characters.reason_removable: One-scene comic foil within a removable side adventure.

minor_characters.name: The Guernsey-man
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chief mate of the Rose-Bud who conspires with Stubb.
minor_characters.reason_removable: One-scene speaker tied to the removable Rose-Bud episode.

minor_characters.name: Captain of the Bachelor
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Jolly captain of a homeward-bound ship met in passing.
minor_characters.reason_removable: The Bachelor gam is thematic counterpoint not required by the synopsis.

minor_characters.name: Captain of the Delight
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Hollow-cheeked captain burying a sailor killed by Moby Dick.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Brief omen-scene; its function (omens before the chase) is already carried by the typhoon, corpusants, and Rachel.

minor_characters.name: Mounttop
minor_characters.appearances_summary: First mate of the Samuel Enderby, named in a parenthetical introduction.
minor_characters.reason_removable: One-line walk-on tied to a removable gam.

subplots.name: The Town-Ho's Story
subplots.reason_removable: An embedded tale told at a Lima inn about a different ship's mutiny; it never affects the Pequod's plot or Ishmael's arc.

subplots.name: Tashtego's fall into the Heidelburgh Tun and Queequeg's rescue
subplots.reason_removable: A self-contained mishap during head-baling that has no later consequences for plot, theme, or character.

subplots.name: Stubb and Flask's Right Whale hunt and superstitions about Fedallah
subplots.reason_removable: Procures the second head for the head-contrast essays but produces no plot beat the synopsis depends on.

subplots.name: The Jungfrau's chase of the old, lame whale and the Fin-Back coda
subplots.reason_removable: The gam itself is in the synopsis ('all brass and emptiness'); the extended kill and aftermath are color that can be trimmed.

subplots.name: The Bulkington apostrophe
subplots.reason_removable: A short eulogy for a character introduced and dropped without consequence.

subplots.name: The Pequod meets the Bouton-de-Rose (Stubb's ambergris swindle)
subplots.reason_removable: A self-contained comic episode whose only consequence (Pip taking an after-oarsman's place) can be relocated as a single sentence.

subplots.name: The Pequod meets the Samuel Enderby
subplots.reason_removable: A duplicative gam: another captain maimed by Moby Dick adds atmosphere but no new plot beat beyond what Jeroboam/Rachel/Delight already supply.

subplots.name: The Pequod meets the Bachelor
subplots.reason_removable: Thematic counterpoint (jolly homeward-bound ship) not required by the synopsis's chain of gams.

subplots.name: Perth the blacksmith's backstory
subplots.reason_removable: A self-contained biographical digression; the forge scene that matters (Ch. 116) stands without it.

subplots.name: The Arsacides whale-skeleton reminiscence
subplots.reason_removable: An embedded travel anecdote unconnected to the Pequod's voyage.
